notes: J0546+0836: counted as follow_up because it is one of the three previously discovered E23 hypervelocity stars (reported space velocities 1500–2800 km s−1) analyzed here (T:p1-b9, T:p1-b14, T:p8-b7); the D6 interpretation remains plausible (T:p10-b7). J0927−6335: same follow_up basis; the D6 interpretation remains plausible (T:p1-b9, T:p1-b14, T:p8-b7, T:p10-b7). J1332−3541: still one of the three E23 hypervelocity stars analyzed here, although the D6 explanation is difficult (T:p1-b9, T:p8-b7, T:p10-b7). J1235-3752: explicitly stated not to be analyzed here, so it is not counted (T:p2-b3).

J0546+0836: The paper reports only a total proper motion for J0546+0836, μ = 76.1 mas yr−1 (T:p8-b5), not separate equatorial components, so no proper_motion_ra or proper_motion_dec values are recorded. No right ascension, declination, or parallax for this target is reported in the supplied material.

J0927−6335: Target star J0927−6335. The paper does not report equatorial coordinates, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probabilities for this star. Two distinct distances are given: an SED-fit spectroscopic distance and a Gaia distance from E23; both are retained. Table 1 gives the Gaia distance as 4.5^{+2.2}_{-1.7} kpc.

J1332−3541: Target star: J1332−3541. The paper reports no right ascension, declination, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for this star. Two distinct distance determinations are retained: the SED spectroscopic distance and the Gaia distance from E23.
